requirements.requirement: Create shared identity dataops with UID/GID 4500 on both node1 and node2
requirements.summary: id dataops on both nodes shows uid=4500(dataops) gid=4500(dataops) groups=4500(dataops), created via matching groupadd/useradd commands.
/etc/exports populated with the share restricted to node2's IP, exportfs -ra applied, exportfs -v confirms active export, and nfs-kernel-server is active with ports 2049/111 listening.

requirements.requirement: Mount the export at /mnt/shared on node2
requirements.summary: showmount confirms the export is visible from node2; mount -a mounts it as nfs4 at /mnt/shared with a persistent /etc/fstab entry added.

requirements.requirement: Shared directory owned dataops:dataops with mode 2770 on both sides
requirements.summary: stat/ls output on node1 shows drwxrws--- dataops dataops (2770) for /srv/nfs/shared, and the same ownership/mode is visible through the mount on node2.

requirements.requirement: Files created on either system keep consistent ownership/permissions (bidirectional access via shared identity)
requirements.summary: dataops user on node2 created from-node2.txt (dataops:dataops), visible from node1, which then created from-node1.txt (dataops:dataops), visible back on node2 with correct ownership on both sides.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are directly and consistently evidenced: the dataops identity (UID/GID 4500) exists on both nodes, /srv/nfs/shared is exported from node1 and mounted at /mnt/shared on node2, the directory carries dataops:dataops 2770 permissions on both sides, and bidirectional file creation under the shared identity preserves consistent ownership. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also executed thoroughly for both nodes: pre-restart healthy baselines, reboot acknowledgements with observed unreachability, changed boot IDs cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and full recovery of the NFS service, export, mount, and prior data (plus a post-reboot write test) were all captured for both node1 and node2, including confirmation that node2's mount survived node1's restart without manual intervention.
limitations: Cannot confirm whether the /tmp/dummy, /tmp/apt-nfs.log, or /tmp/reboot.log temp files were explicitly cleaned up versus implicitly cleared by the two reboots, since the after-executor temporary-files inventory may be bounded/filtered.
No test was captured of a non-dataops user being denied access (mode 2770 group-restriction), though this was not explicitly required by the task.

operational_hygiene.summary: One exploratory command (cmd-cb645cb6eeb047d5) wrote a throwaway file to /tmp/dummy purely to preview an export line and check env vars before the real /etc/exports was written in a separate command (cmd-ff18a9696a3a4192); this /tmp/dummy content had no causal role in the final configuration and its removal is not evidenced. Transient /tmp/apt-nfs.log and /tmp/reboot.log files from package installs and reboot scheduling are also not confirmed removed, though the after-executor temporary-files inventory (which lists only systemd-private-* entries on both nodes) suggests /tmp was effectively reset by the reboots. All other state-changing commands (user/group creation, package install, directory/permission setup, exports config, service enable, mount setup, file writes, and the two node reboots) map directly to a material outcome or the required restart-evidence protocol. No destructive, broad, or security-weakening mutations were observed.
